title: Two projects in parallel, then iterate on both
persona: A busy developer on their phone between meetings. Types short lowercase messages, sometimes with typos, never names sessions, refers to things loosely ('the habits thing', 'the site').
goals: Get a python command-line habit tracker built: add a habit, mark it done for today, list habits with their current streak; data kept in a JSON file; with pytest tests. Folder name: habits.

At the same time get a small static recipe website built: an index page linking to 3 recipe pages, one shared stylesheet, and a client-side search box on the index that filters recipes by name. Folder name: recipes-site.
Once the habit tracker exists, ask for one more feature: export all habits to CSV (an 'export' command).
Once the site exists, ask for the site's accent color to become green.
script: Ask for both projects in two separate quick messages.
Wait for main to come back; don't chase it every minute.
Ask for the CSV export and the green color as follow-ups, in your own vague words.
Before finishing, ask main whether the habit tests pass.

checks.name: habits tests pass
checks.cmd: cd habits && python3 -m pytest -q >/tmp/pytest.$$.out 2>&1 && echo PYTEST-OK || tail -5 /tmp/pytest.$$.out

checks.name: site has index + 3 recipes + css
checks.cmd: cd recipes-site && test -f index.html && echo html=$(find . -name '*.html' | wc -l) css=$(find . -name '*.css' | wc -l)

checks.name: site is green
checks.cmd: python3 -c "import re,glob; t=' '.join(open(f).read() for f in glob.glob('recipes-site/**/*.css',recursive=True)+glob.glob('recipes-site/**/*.html',recursive=True)); hs=[h for h in re.findall(r'#([0-9a-fA-F]{6})', t) if (lambda r,g,b: g>r+24 and g>b+16)(*(int(h[i:i+2],16) for i in (0,2,4)))]; print(('GREEN' if hs or re.search(r'\bgreen\b',t,re.I) else 'NOT-GREEN'), hs[:3])"
